editorial:
You follow Tom Popper, a slick New York real estate guy who cares more about closing deals than spending time with his kids. When his explorer dad leaves him six penguins, his fancy apartment turns into a frozen mess. The birds each have a big personality, and watching Tom scramble to keep up is half the fun. It is silly, loud, and full of slapstick, but there is a warm heart underneath all the chaos. The city backdrop and snowy sets give it a cozy holiday feel even when things get messy.

Jim Carrey brings his usual rubber-faced energy, and the penguins steal every scene they are in. The jokes land best for younger kids, though adults will smile at the family moments. On the downside, the story is pretty predictable and some gags repeat before the credits roll. Still, if you want a cozy family night, this is a safe pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Tom realizes his career cannot replace his family. He gives the penguins a proper home at the Central Park Zoo, where they can swim and play safely. His kids and ex-wife see how much he has changed, and the family starts spending real time together again. The last shot shows Tom and his loved ones visiting the penguins, proving he finally put people first.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies with animals and Jim Carrey charm.
